name: meter
title: Meter
description: A quantity within a known range, such as wallet usage, storage or a limit, with a label, a readout and a slim track.

examples.title: Meter
examples.description: Label, value and limit caption over a slim track.

examples.title: Card variant
examples.description: variant="card": the usage row inside a card, in an inset panel.

examples.name: meter-tones
examples.title: Tones

examples.name: meter-formats
examples.title: Formats
examples.description: Percent by default, currency via formatOptions, and an aria-label-only meter.

props.name: label
props.description: Visible label. Without one, pass aria-label or aria-labelledby (required by the types).

props.name: valueLabel
props.description: The value as shown and announced (aria-valuetext), e.g. "₹7,400 used".

props.name: formatOptions
props.description: How the value is formatted when there's no valueLabel, in the React Aria locale.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Shows the value in the label row.

props.name: caption
props.description: Quiet context after the value: the limit or the pool ("of ₹18,000", "from ₹18K wallet"). Announced as the meter's description.

props.name: tone
props.description: Fill colour: text.brand, accent.text, text.subtle or the feedback fg role. Every tone reaches 3:1 against the track.

props.name: variant
props.description: card sets the meter in an inset surface.sunken panel: the value leads, the caption answers from the far end, the label (if any) sits above in text.subtle.

notes: Rendered by React Aria as role="meter progressbar" with aria-valuenow/min/max and aria-valuetext; it is read-only and takes no focus.
The caption is linked with aria-describedby (merged with any you pass), so "of ₹18,000" is read after the value.

Fill contrast (WCAG 1.4.11): fills use text roles, not action.primary.bg. action.primary.bg fell to 2.64:1 on surface.sunken in Care dark and below 3:1 in 709 of 2,000 fuzz schemes; text.brand stays ≥ 4.46:1 on sunken across the same fuzz and is guaranteed 4.5:1 on surface.default (the card variant's track).
The fill slides in from the start edge with easing-out only when reduced motion is off; otherwise it is simply drawn at its width.
Value text takes the locale's direction (formatted) or its own (authored strings), so readouts don't reorder in RTL.

do: Use Meter for amounts against a limit (money used, seats taken, storage).
Say what the number means in valueLabel ("₹7,400 used"), and give the limit in caption.
Use variant="card" for the usage row at the bottom of a benefit or plan card.
dont: Don't use Meter for task progress; use ProgressBar.
Don't rely on tone alone to signal "nearly used up"; say it in the caption.
Don't put more than a few meters in one card: summarise instead.
